questions.model:
Multiply both sides by 15: 5(x + 7) = 3(2x − 1)
5x + 35 = 6x − 3
38 = x, so x = 38.
questions.tip: Cross-multiplying puts each numerator in a bracket: 5(x + 7), not 5x + 7.

questions.q: Make h the subject of the formula A = 2πr² + 2πrh.
ms: A1: h = (A − 2πr²)/(2πr) oe, e.g. h = A/(2πr) − r
questions.tip: Subtract the term without h first, then divide by everything multiplying h.

questions.q:
Solve the simultaneous equations. You must show all your working.
5x + 2y = 3
3x − 4y = 20
ms: M1: multiplies one or both equations to make the coefficients of one variable equal, e.g. 10x + 4y = 6
M1: correctly adds/subtracts to eliminate one variable, e.g. 13x = 26
questions.model:
Multiply the first equation by 2: 10x + 4y = 6
Add to 3x − 4y = 20: 13x = 26, so x = 2.
Substitute: 5(2) + 2y = 3 → 2y = −7 → y = −3.5.
Check in the second equation: 3(2) − 4(−3.5) = 6 + 14 = 20 ✓
questions.tip: Different signs on the y-terms, so add the equations.

questions.q:
A rectangle has length (3x − 2) cm and width (x + 4) cm. Its perimeter is 52 cm.
(a) Write down an equation in x and solve it. [3]
(b) Find the area of the rectangle. [1]
ms: (b) B1: 160 cm² FT their x if positive lengths
questions.tip: Perimeter uses both lengths and both widths; using only one of each halves your equation.

questions.q: Make x the subject of the formula y = √((x + 2)/(x − 3)).
ms: M1: y²(x − 3) = x + 2 (multiplies out the fraction)
M1: collects the x terms on one side, e.g. xy² − x = 3y² + 2
questions.model:
Square both sides: y² = (x + 2)/(x − 3)
Multiply by (x − 3): xy² − 3y² = x + 2
Collect x terms: xy² − x = 3y² + 2
Factorise: x(y² − 1) = 3y² + 2
x = (3y² + 2)/(y² − 1)
questions.tip: When the subject appears twice, collect both x terms on one side and then factorise x out.

questions.q:
Solve the simultaneous equations.
y = 2x + 1
xy = 15
ms: M1: correct factorisation (2x − 5)(x + 3) or correct formula substitution
questions.tip: Give the answers as pairs; a lone list of x values loses the final marks.
